explanation: A machine that helps us write, draw, play and learn. It follows the instructions we give it, one by one, very quickly.
match: The whole machine that puts all the parts together to work.

explanation: The part of the computer where we see pictures, letters and videos. It's how the computer shows us what it's doing.
It has lots of keys with letters and numbers. We press them to type words into the computer.
match: You type letters and numbers with it.

explanation: The device we move with our hand to point at and click on things we see on the screen.
match: Points and clicks on the screen.

explanation: All the parts of a computer we can actually touch, like the screen, keyboard and mouse.
match: The parts you can touch with your hand.

explanation: The programs that tell a computer what to do. You can't touch them, but they make the computer work and do things.
A small program made for one task, like drawing, playing a game or listening to music.
Where we save a piece of work, a drawing or a photo on the computer, so we can open it again later.
Used to keep several files together, just like a folder keeps several sheets of paper together.
A huge network that connects computers all around the world, so we can see webpages, send messages and learn new things.
A way to connect a computer or phone to the internet without using any wires.
The program we use to open and view webpages, like a window into the online world.
A page we can visit on the internet, full of text, pictures or videos about a topic.
A secret made of letters and numbers that protects our accounts. Never share it with friends or strangers — only with a parent.
Your full name, address, school or photos are private. Never share them online without talking to an adult first.
If something online makes you feel confused, scared or strange, always tell a trusted adult. Never keep it a secret by yourself.
Not everything we see on the internet is true. Before believing or sharing something, it's worth asking an adult or checking somewhere else.
Screens are fun, but our bodies also need to play outside, read books and rest our eyes. Balance is the key!
A way to store files and photos on a very large computer, far from home, so we can open them from any device connected to the internet.
Hardware is the parts you touch, like the screen or mouse. Software is the programs you can't touch, but that make everything work inside.

term: Turn it off and on again
explanation: When a device misbehaves or freezes, often the first thing to try is turning it off and back on. It fixes many small problems!
Everything you post or search online leaves a trail, like footprints in the sand. That's why it's worth thinking before sharing something.
Every once in a while programs get improvements and fixes, called updates, so they work better and safer.
Using screens with an adult nearby, taking breaks, and always with a purpose (learning, creating, talking to family) helps keep a good balance.
